blocks.h2: Switching a Skokie Fireplace to Gas Logs
blocks.body: Many 1950s Skokie homes have a brick fireplace in the living room. Switching to gas logs means no wood to carry and no ash to clean. We run the gas line, install a shutoff valve near the fireplace and set the log set. A chimney professional should inspect the flue first. Vented logs need the damper held partly open, so we install a clamp.

blocks.h2: What Affects the Price of Fireplace Work
blocks.body: A service visit is simple. A failed part depends on the fireplace. A gas log conversion depends on how far the line has to run. We diagnose and quote a flat price.

blocks.h2: Gas Fireplace Questions From Skokie Homeowners

items.q: Why are my gas logs leaving soot?
items.preview: Logs out of position or a dirty burner.
items.answer: Usually the logs aren't in the right position or the burner needs cleaning. We clean and reset them.

items.q: Does the damper need to stay open with gas logs?
items.answer: Yes. Vented gas logs need the damper held partly open so exhaust can leave.

items.q: Why won't my pilot stay lit?
items.preview: Usually a dirty pilot or weak thermocouple.
items.answer: Usually the pilot is dirty or the thermocouple is weak. Cleaning or replacing the part fixes it.
Early fall, before the first cold night.

items.q: Can I add a remote to my gas logs?
items.answer: Often, with a compatible valve. We'll check your model.
